prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1337; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss came in from the policyholder's side after a side impact at a signalized intersection, with the claimant listed as a passenger in the vehicle struck on the driver's side. The claimant is represented by counsel, so all further contact will be routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time of the collision. Nothing in the file points to any damage existing before coverage began.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene and describes the crash in line with the initial account. Officer notes were consistent with the driver's statement.

Entry 4: Spoke with the other driver, who gave the same description of the light sequence and the point of impact. Their account matches what was reported at first notice.

Entry 5: Reviewed scene photos and the vehicle damage profile. The crush pattern and panel damage line up with a side impact of the type described.

Entry 6: Collected statements from two independent witnesses. Both recall the collision and the vehicle positions the same way the other parties have described them.

Entry 7: Claimant's counsel sent the initial medical summary reporting a concussion diagnosed at the emergency department after the crash. The injury profile fits the force and direction of the impact.

Entry 8: Requested prior medical records. No earlier injury to the same body area appears in the history provided, and the claimant reports no prior head trauma.

Entry 9: Treatment followed a typical course, with follow-up visits and symptom checks that gradually decreased as the claimant improved. Treating provider notes show steady recovery.

Entry 10: Spoke with the claimant through counsel. The account of the crash, including the sequence and seating position, was the same as in every earlier conversation.

Entry 11: Reviewed repair estimates and the shop's inspection. No earlier damage to the vehicle is recorded, and the repairs address only the collision damage.

Entry 12: Current status: liability and damage are established, the bodily injury claim is being evaluated based on the medical record, and the file is set for counsel's demand package.
